symptom: `mxcli check -p` of one microflow took 1.4 s on a project of 1,719 units with pages, and the time grew with the number of stored pages whatever the script held (ako/mxcli#2160, mendixlabs/mxcli#1842).
cause: loadStoredUses decoded every stored page, snippet, layout, nanoflow, menu and the navigation document into bson.D to collect the strings under "Microflow"/"Nanoflow" keys. A page decodes into tens of thousands of values; the decode was 1.07 s of the 1.45 s.
file: mdl/executor/validate_flow_access.go (storedUses, rawFlowRefs; storedUsesDecoded kept as the test's oracle)
fix: Walk the raw bytes with bsoncore.ReadElement and keep only the string values under the two keys; read Name and Excluded with Lookup. 1.37 s -> 0.54 s, identical check output.
insight: The CPU profile could not name the caller: a page is deeper than Go's 64-frame profile stack, so the decode showed as 54% of samples under no executor function and the check that owned it showed as 7%. Wall-clock timers around each check phase settled it in one run. Also: the earlier guess that this was the fixed cost on the 5,373-unit filler project was wrong -- that project has few pages, and there it was 0.1 s. Measure on a project that has the document type before naming the cost.
test: mdl/executor/stored_uses_pedapp_test.go: differential against the decoding form on every source document of the fixture plus a page calling a microflow and a nanoflow and an excluded page, with assertions that the fixture exercised it; synthetic shapes; allocations of scan vs decode. Four mutations each fail.
